title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost across common workloads by providing safe, production-ready autotune defaults for batching and KV-caching, ship model quantization profiles, and add end-to-end unit-economics tooling. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) an autotuner that observes request latency/throughput and recommends per-model batch_size and max_latency SLOs, with safe defaults that prioritize p99 latency; 2) updated KV-cache and prefix-caching defaults to improve cold-start cost without impacting correctness; 3) a set of empirically-validated quantization profiles for curated LLMs (4-bit/8-bit tradeoffs) and a new unit-economics service that simulates per-token cost under different config combinations. Checklist: - [x] implement autotuner core loop and expose REST config API - [x] add persistent default profiles (runtime/kv_cache/defaults.yaml) - [x] add quantization profiles for models in model-catalog (runtime/quant/profiles.yaml) - [x] integrate unit-econ tooling and a simple UI endpoint (tools/uecon/service.py) - [x] update SDK defaults (sdk/python/redwood/params.py) - [x] unit + integration tests (tests/test_autotune.py) - [x] docs and runbook (docs/cost-optimizations.md). Testing & results: integrated canary run on dedicated pool with 1M synthetic requests showed 18% token-cost reduction and p99 latency within 5% of baseline when using autotune + cache defaults; quant profiles yielded 22-35% memory reduction with <1.5% degradation in generation quality (per eval suite). Rollout plan: feature gated behind org-level opt-in flag; rolling canary in prod for low-traffic orgs for 2 weeks then broader rollout. Related: Linear ENG-2381 (autotune), ENG-2410 (unit econ), touches model-catalog onboarding flow. Breaking change: none (all changes behind flags; quant profiles opt-in per model).
